cover_letter_text:
Hi Jaydo team,

I'm Marc, and I'd like a site engineer role in your Urban Development team. I studied civil engineering in the Philippines, finishing in 2019, and graduated here in February 2026 with an Advanced Diploma of Civil Construction Design. Your advert says it's hands-on, on site with the supervisors and crews, so I wanted to apply.

From April 2019 to February 2020 I worked on site in the Philippines. On a community hall renovation I coordinated 10 to 15 workers each day and checked the work against the drawings. On subdivision finishing works I helped with quality checks and wrote the site reports.

I live in Melton, I have my own car and a White Card, and I can start two weeks after an offer. I've got full working rights in Australia (Subclass 485 visa). Happy to talk whenever suits.

Kind regards,
Marc Masarate

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
options: I'm a permanent resident and/or NZ citizen
I have a family/partner visa with no restrictions
I have a graduate temporary work visa
I have a holiday temporary work visa
I have a temporary visa with restrictions on work location (e.g. skilled regional visa 491)
I have a temporary protection or safe haven enterprise work visa
I have a temporary visa with no restrictions (e.g. doctoral student)
I have a temporary visa with restrictions on work hours (e.g. student visa, retirement visa)
I have a temporary visa with restrictions on industry (e.g. temporary activity visa 408)
I require sponsorship to work for a new employer (e.g. 482, 457)
questions.answer: I have a graduate temporary work visa

questions.question: Do you hold a Construction Induction Safety certificate (White Card)?
Do you have a current Australian driver's licence?
